[**Ocean Ridge**](https://www.lxhausys.com/us/products/viatera-quartz-surface/ocean-ridge/513261)

Flowing with the rhythm of the sea, Ocean Ridge captures the meeting of deep navy and sunlit hues. Fine navy veins ripple alongside soft, shadowy waves that drift across an off-white foundation, expressing the quiet movement of tides. Reflecting both the delicacy and strength of the ocean’s edge, it brings a calm, living energy to any space. Ocean Ridge is made in the U.S. and is BABA compliant. It is available in 2- and 3-centimeter thicknesses with a polished finish in a 63-by-130-inch slab size.

**Two new colors join the VIATERA Masterpiece Collection:**

[**Midnight Ember Brushed**](https://www.lxhausys.com/us/products/viatera-quartz-surface/midnight-ember-brushed/513263)

Glowing with the quiet intensity of its name, Midnight Ember Brushed emanates depth and refined warmth. Refined veins of gold and white flicker across a foundation of warm black, recalling the final embers glowing in the night. Mysterious yet inviting, it grounds any space with quiet strength. [**Winter Grove**](https://www.lxhausys.com/us/products/viatera-quartz-surface/winter-grove/513265)

Peaceful and contemplative, Winter Grove evokes the stillness of a snow-covered forest. Beneath its white expanse, soft hints of sage green and delicate shadow-like veins emerge, mirroring the quiet patterns of branches in winter light. Gentle and grounding, it offers a comforting presence for interiors that invite rest and reflection. Winter Grove features a polished finish and incorporates LX Hausys’ NeoQ technology. It is available in 2- and 3-centimeter thicknesses in a 63-by-126-inch slab size.

**Two new colors join the VIATERA Quartzite Collection:**

[**Perla Verde**](https://www.lxhausys.com/us/products/viatera-quartz-surface/perla-verde/513269)

Reminiscent of seawater tracing elegant patterns in the sand, Perla Verde reveals a soft gray foundation touched with sage green and crossed by veins of deep green and brown. Its organic, layered beauty reflects the rhythm of nature, offering a neutral palette that feels balanced, sophisticated, and full of depth. Perla Verde features a polished finish and incorporates LX Hausys’ TrueView and NeoQ technologies. It is available in 2- and 3-centimeter thicknesses in a 63-by-126-inch slab size.

[**Crystallo Vera**](https://www.lxhausys.com/us/products/viatera-quartz-surface/crystallo-vera/513267)

Inspired by remote, untouched glaciers and the clarity of natural quartzite, Crystallo Vera embodies refined simplicity. Its crystal-like white surface reveals subtle tone-on-tone variations that create a luminous, translucent impression. Versatile and balanced, it complements both cool and warm design schemes with timeless grace. Crystallo Vera features a polished finish and incorporates LX Hausys’ TrueView and NeoQ technologies. It is available in 2- and 3-centimeter thicknesses in a 63-by-126-inch slab size.

All colors are backed by LX Hausys’ 15-year limited warranty.

The VIATERA brand is defined by its classic and timeless aesthetic, inspired by the earth’s natural splendor. Consisting of seven collections offering a wide variety of hues and patterns for any kitchen or bath application, VIATERA surfaces contain up to 93% quartz—one of the hardest minerals on earth. Providing exceptional durability, high resistance to stains and ease of maintenance, all VIATERA colors come with multiple independent certifications verifying their environmental and health benefits. These include Declare, Red List Free, GREENGUARD, EPD and HPD certifications.

LX Hausys established its first quartz manufacturing plant in the U.S. in Adairsville, Ga., in 2010. Today, the company operates three production lines within a facility spanning more than 293,000 square feet that employs more than 160 associates. LX Hausys is the only manufacturer in the U.S. with a plant that produces both solid surface and quartz in the same location. LX Hausys’ nearby Central Distribution Center serves regional warehouses throughout the U.S. and Canada, enabling fast and efficient product availability. The company’s commitment to U.S.-based manufacturing supports its sustainability goals by minimizing environmental impact associated with long-distance and international transportation.

For more information, visit [lxhausys.com.](https://www.lxhausys.com/us/index)

LX Hausys America Inc. is a part of Korean-based LX Hausys Ltd., one of the world’s leading providers of building and decorative materials employing more than 4,300 employees spanning the globe. Headquartered in Atlanta, Ga., LX Hausys America uses the industry’s most advanced technology and eco-friendly manufacturing processes to design products that help create beautiful and functional spaces. # EXHIBITOR NEWS

# LX Hausys Debuts Four New HIMACS Colors at KBIS 2026

Feb 17, 2026

![](https://kbis.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/Calacatta-Full-Moon-M812-Lobby-desk-mid-scaled.jpg)

**ORLANDO, Fla.** – [The Kitchen & Bath Industry Show (KBIS)](https://kbis.com/) – Feb. 17, 2026 – [LX Hausys America Inc.](https://www.lxhausys.com/us/index) (Booth #W1429), an innovative manufacturer of building and decorative materials, is introducing four new HIMACS solid surface colors at this year’s KBIS. Designed for commercial and residential interiors, the new colors reflect the stunning visual looks needed for today’s modern environments ranging from hospitality and wellness areas to retail and workplace settings. Expanding the HIMACS Calacatta and Terrazzo collections, the new colors also bring superior durability, easy cleanability and dynamic thermoforming capabilities, allowing designers the freedom to create the expressive surface designs they envision.

“Commercial interior designers are looking for surfaces that can help them achieve their design visions, whether that’s making a statement for a reception area or providing a sense of calm for a spa,” said Mike Morici, vice president of surfaces sales and channel management at LX Hausys America. “These new HIMACS colors deliver all of that, and more. From refined Italian Calacatta stone to the timeless look of Terrazzo, these colors offer a thoughtful balance of natural inspiration and refined aesthetics. Their design versatility, coupled with their superior, long-lasting performance, make them the ideal solution for any commercial interior.”

**Two new colors join the [HIMACS Calacatta](https://www.lxhausys.com/us/products/himacs-solid-surface) Collection:**

[**Calacatta Full Moon**](https://www.lxhausys.com/us/products/himacs-solid-surface/calacatta-full-moon/513212)

Calacatta Full Moon features long, flowing veins of varying thickness that move harmoniously across a rich cream-toned base. Subtle tonal variations and organic movement evoke the natural artistry of Italian stone, while a faint, light-catching sparkle follows the veining, adding depth and a gentle, vein-traced radiance. The result is a surface that feels both lively and refined, creating a warm, inviting atmosphere suited to elegant residential interiors and elevated commercial environments alike. Calacatta Full Moon is available in 30-by-145-inch sheets with a 1/2-inch thickness.

[**Calacatta Snow Moon**](https://www.lxhausys.com/us/products/himacs-solid-surface/calacatta-snow-moon/513275)

Calacatta Snow Moon presents a soft, light-toned base accented by a balanced interplay of thin and bold veining, forming a sophisticated Calacatta pattern. A delicate, luminous shimmer is infused into the base, capturing and diffusing light for a calm, glowing effect, while the veining stays crisp and understated. Blending natural stone authenticity with contemporary refinement, this design delivers timeless elegance and serene beauty for spaces that seek understated luxury. Calacatta Snow Moon is available in 30-by-145-inch sheets with a 1/2-inch thickness.

**Two new colors join the HIMACS Terrazzo Collection:**

[**Terrazzo Ulivo**](https://www.lxhausys.com/us/products/himacs-solid-surface/terrazzo-ulivo/513201)

Terrazzo Ulivo features an off-white base accented with terrazzo speckles in natural olive and gray-green tones. Inspired by traditional Italian terrazzo incorporating olive stone fragments, this color brings a sense of heritage and artisanal craftsmanship to any space. Its earthy hues echo the serene beauty of Mediterranean olive groves, where silvery-green foliage sways gently in the breeze. Blending classic elegance with organic charm, Terrazzo Ulivo delivers a calm, timeless finish. Terrazzo Ulivo is available in 30-by-145-inch sheets with a 1/2-inch thickness.

[**Terrazzo Nuvola**](https://www.lxhausys.com/us/products/himacs-solid-surface/terrazzo-nuvola/513200)

Terrazzo Nuvola combines light, cloud-like chips with deeper tones that evoke wildflowers in a pine forest. Inspired by the delicate beauty of flowers in bloom, it captures the essence of nature in motion. Its warm, nostalgic mood is infused with lively charm, making it perfect for interiors that exude romance and grace. With its gentle yet expressive pattern, Terrazzo Nuvola’s sophistication is further enhanced by the timeless appeal of terrazzo. Terrazzo Nuvola is available in 30-by-145-inch sheets with a 1/2-inch thickness

All colors are backed by LX Hausys’ 15-year limited warranty.

HIMACS is a durable, nonporous solid surface material made from a blend of acrylic, natural minerals and pigments. Seamless, repairable and hygienic, HIMACS is ideal for a wide range of interior applications, from countertops and wall panels to custom furniture and commercial surfaces. Its thermoformable properties enable creative freedom in design, while a wide palette of colors and patterns—including natural stone looks, solid hues and terrazzo—offers extensive aesthetic versatility. HIMACS surfaces are GREENGUARD and NSF certified.

LX Hausys established its first solid surface manufacturing plant in the U.S. in Adairsville, Ga., in 2005. Today, the company operates three production lines within a facility spanning more than 293,000 square feet that employs more than 160 associates. LX Hausys is the only manufacturer in the U.S. with a plant that produces both solid surface and quartz in the same location. LX Hausys’ nearby Central Distribution Center serves regional warehouses throughout the U.S. and Canada, enabling fast and efficient product availability. The company’s commitment to U.S.-based manufacturing supports its sustainability goals by minimizing environmental impact associated with long-distance and international transportation.

For more information, visit [lxhausys.com.](http://www.lxhausys.com./)

**About LX Hausys America Inc.**

LX Hausys America Inc. is a part of Korean-based LX Hausys Ltd., one of the world’s leading providers of building and decorative materials employing more than 4,300 employees spanning the globe. Headquartered in Atlanta, Ga., LX Hausys America uses the industry’s most advanced technology and eco-friendly manufacturing processes to design products that help create beautiful and functional spaces. Architects, designers, flooring professionals, and other trade professionals looking for more information can visit [www.lxhausys.com.](http://www.lxhausys.com./)

# EXHIBITOR NEWS

# LX Hausys Debuts BORTE Premium Panel System at KBIS

Feb 17, 2026

![](https://kbis.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/Kitchen-UNQ05-NTR10-Mid-scaled.jpg)

**ORLANDO, Fla.** – [The Kitchen & Bath Industry Show (KBIS)](https://kbis.com/) – Feb. 17, 2026 – [LX Hausys America Inc.](https://www.lxhausys.com/us/index) (Booth #W1429), an innovative manufacturer of building and decorative materials, is launching a new premium panel system, BORTE, at this year’s KBIS. Bringing the innovative design, advanced technology and sustainability benefits for which LX Hausys is known, BORTE offers residential and commercial design professionals a new option for reimagining kitchen, bathroom and other spaces with elevated aesthetics, exceptional durability and easy maintenance.

[BORTE](https://www.lxhausys.com/us/products/borte-panel) is debuting with three distinctive collections and its Complete Product Program, a suite of edgebands, films, profiles and foil that perfectly coordinate with the panels. Each element of the program allows for a seamless and consistent design throughout any space while offering greater design diversity and a premium quality look. All BORTE edgebands are precisely color-matched to the panel colors and are available in PUR/EVA and Zero-joint edge types in widths of 22mm, 41mm and 45mm.

BORTE’s three debuting collections were developed by LX Hausys’ internationally renowned and award-winning Global Design Team based in Seoul, South Korea. Drawing on their extensive global trend research capabilities and U.S. customer feedback, the perfectly curated mix of patterns, hues and textures across the three collections capture the design desires of homeowners today, making BORTE an ideal solution for cabinets, closets, furniture and other applications across an array of interiors.

The new BORTE colors span three distinct collections. The Reserve Collection, available in nine colors, celebrates surfaces shaped by texture, detail and craftsmanship. Inspired by hand-worked materials and refined finishes, each option highlights depth, movement and character designed to be seen, touched and lived with. The Hue Collection, available in 20 colors, explores color as atmosphere, from quiet neutrals to deeper, more expressive tones. Inspired by light, landscape and everyday environments, each shade is designed to shape mood, enhance space, and create a feeling of calm confidence in modern interiors. The Origin Collection is rooted in the modern sophistication of natural materials, drawing from woods, soft finishes, and enduring forms. Available in 18 colors, these surfaces bring warmth and balance to interiors, creating spaces that feel grounded, welcoming, and thoughtfully composed. BORTE panels are being stocked at LX Hausys’ Central Distribution Center in Adairsville, Ga., allowing for quick delivery throughout the U.S., Mexico and Canada.

Every BORTE surface features LX Hausys’ Super Matte Resistant (SMR) technology. SMR is an industry-leading coating innovation that brings a refined aesthetic and an embossed, tailored texture to create an authentic feel. Proven in tests to prevent stains, scratches and fingerprint smudges, BORTE surfaces with SMR technology meet the highest levels of design and durability, and allow for easy maintenance.

“A premium panel can greatly enhance the look and feel of a kitchen, bath or living space, instantly adding value and personal satisfaction,” said K.T. Kang, business director of LX Hausys BORTE Panel. “Expertly designed and featuring our SMR technology, these collections will immediately show designers, homebuilders and homeowners how our BORTE panel system can elevate any space.”

BORTE supports healthier indoor environments through its GREENGUARD Gold certification and its CARB P2 certification for low formaldehyde emissions. For customers seeking sustainable options, BORTE panels can be requested with a bio-based coating. Customers can also request BORTE panels come with the polymer film containing post-consumer recycled content.

BORTE panels are manufactured using a medium-density fiberboard (MDF) core bonded with environmentally friendly glue and a high-performance polymer film with trend-setting designs laminated on the surface, while the back side is finished with a low-pressure melamine (LPM). The result is a product that offers greater cost, stability, performance and design advantages over wood and other similar products such as TFL, HPL or high-performance HPL. BORTE surfaces come in a 4-by-8-foot panel size and 18 mm thick.

Designers, home builders and others can learn more about BORTE at [lxhausys.com/us/products/borte-panel](https://www.lxhausys.com/us/products/borte-panel). BORTE samples can be requested by contacting the BORTE Product Management Team at [jooheecha@lxhausys.com](mailto:jooheecha@lxhausys.com).

**About LX Hausys America Inc.**

[LX Hausys America Inc.](https://www.lxhausys.com./gl/index) is a part of Korean-based LX Hausys Ltd., one of the world’s leading providers of building and decorative materials employing more than 4,300 employees spanning the globe. Headquartered in metro Atlanta, Ga., LX Hausys America uses the industry’s most advanced technology and eco-friendly manufacturing processes to design products that help create beautiful and functional spaces. Architects, designers, flooring professionals, and other trade professionals looking for more information can visit [www.lxhausys.com.](https://www.lxhausys.com./gl/index)

![](https://kbis.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/TR-24REF-L-SG-A305-H04_TRL_HR-scaled.jpeg)

[True Caliber](https://true-caliber.com/), where professional-grade refrigeration meets precision grilling for the luxury home, proudly unveils its 2026 Color of the Year: Espresso. A deep, full-bodied brown with subtle velvet undertones, Espresso joins True Caliber’s expansive collection of finishes as a sophisticated, dark neutral.

Reminiscent of a perfectly pulled ristretto, Espresso delivers richness and depth without visual weight, adding warmth and balance to both modern and classic spaces. Unlike a standard brown, this nuanced finish possesses a sense of permanence and quiet luxury, pairing effortlessly with natural materials, warm metals, and layered textures.

“Espresso was designed to offer a sense of stability and focus within the home,” remarks Chelsea Bothe, Brand & Marketing Manager at True Caliber. “It exudes a refined and understated elegance, yielding a finish that feels intentional and effortlessly at home in any well-designed kitchen. Whether anchoring a bright, modern space or enriching a traditional one, Espresso transforms any space into an inviting sanctuary that is both contemporary and enduring.”

The new hue’s ability to convey a sense of ease and polish makes it an ideal fit for both interior kitchens and outdoor entertaining suites. As with all True Caliber finishes, Espresso is available across the full range of full-size and indoor/outdoor undercounter refrigeration units and grills, allowing for seamless integration throughout the home.

The addition of the Espresso colorway, along with the reintroduction of its legacy Crimson finish, to True Caliber’s Build Your True Program of curated custom finish and hardware options, now allows designers and homeowners a choice of 96 alluring color combinations. These standard finishes include Olive, Champagne, Bluestone, Sage, Juniper, Gloss Black, Matte Black, Ultra Matte Black, Emerald, Cobalt, Matte White, Antique White, Stainless Steel, and the aforementioned Crimson. Complementary hardware options include Stainless Steel, Copper, Brass, Pewter, Gold, and Chrome.

# Nice Expands U.S. Representation with Thomasson Marketing Group

New Nice partnership with Thomasson Marketing Group strengthens dealer support and drives growth for 2GIG solutions.

Published: June 12, 2026SSI Staff

\[display\_gallery\_copyright\_text\]

![Nice Thomasson](<Base64-Image-Removed>)

Image courtesy of Nice

**CARLSBAD, Calif. —** Smart home and business solutions provider [Nice](https://www.securitysales.com/tag/nice/) recentlyannounced a [new partnership](https://www.niceforyou.com/na/for-partners) with Thomasson Marketing Group, Inc. (TMG), further strengthening Nice North America’s regional representation and support for its 2GIG security solutions across the Pacific Western United States.

Working closely with Nice’s regional sales managers (RSMs), TMG “will provide local dealers and distribution partners with an additional layer of field support, resources and expertise,” according to the company announcement.

This strategic partnership “reinforces Nice North America’s ongoing commitment to expanding localized sales expertise, dealer engagement and market development within the security and smart home channel,” the announcement says.

## Why Did Nice Partner with Thomasson Marketing Group?

“Regional representation plays a critical role in how we support our partners and drive growth in key markets,” says Donnie McVicker, chief sales officer of Nice North America, in the company announcement. “Thomasson Marketing Group brings strong relationships, deep industry knowledge, and a proven ability to execute at the local level.

![SSI Newsletter](<Base64-Image-Removed>)

“Their focus on dealer engagement and sell-through initiatives will help expand the reach of our 2GIG portfolio and support our partners’ success across this important region,” he says.

With this partnership, Thomasson Marketing Group will represent 2GIG solutions across Alaska, Arizona, California, Colorado, Hawaii, Idaho, Montana, New Mexico, Nevada, Oregon, Utah, Washington and Wyoming, the announcement says.

Led by president Jordan R. Thomasson, TMG “has built a strong reputation for delivering strategic sales representation and channel development within the security and low voltage electronics industries,” according to the company announcement.

Through this relationship, Nice North America “continues to invest in its regional representation strategy, ensuring dealers and distributors have access to the resources, expertise and support needed to succeed in an increasingly competitive market,” the announcement says.

“We’re excited to partner with Nice North America and represent the 2GIG portfolio across such a dynamic region,” says Thomasson in the announcement. “2GIG continues to be a trusted name in the security and smart home space, and we look forward to helping dealers grow their businesses through strong local support and market development.”

# IQSIGHT Appoints Wilkinson as Vice President of Sales, North America

Wilkinson will be responsible for accelerating IQSIGHT's sales growth and deepening engagement with its channel partners and customers.

Published: June 11, 2026SSI Staff

\[display\_gallery\_copyright\_text\]

![IQSIGHT Wilkinson](<Base64-Image-Removed>)

Photo courtesy of IQSIGHT

- _IQSIGHT recently announced Ted Wilkinson as vice president of sales, North America_
- _Wilkinson will be responsible for accelerating sales growth, executing regional go-to-market strategy and deepening engagement with IQSIGHT’s channel partners and customers_
- _He has more than three decades of experience in the technology sector_

**EINDHOVEN, Netherlands —** Global intelligence-first video security provider [IQSIGHT](https://www.securitysales.com/tag/iqsight/) recently announced that security and technology industry leader Ted Wilkinson has joined its executive team as [vice president of sales, North America.](https://www.iqsight.com/en/contact/)

In his new role, Wilkinson “will be responsible for accelerating sales growth, executing regional go-to-market strategy and deepening engagement with IQSIGHT’s channel partners and customers,” the company announcement says.

“Ted brings the right combination of industry insight and execution expertise to lead our North American team and align the regional sales efforts with our broader global strategy,” says Sam Ward, chief commercial officer, global sales, at IQSIGHT, in the announcement.

“He is committed to cultivating loyalty with our channel partners and customers by empowering the sales team

to meet market needs and unlock new opportunities for growth,” he says.

![SSI Newsletter](<Base64-Image-Removed>)

## Why Did IQSIGHT Add Ted Wilkinson?

Wilkinson has more than three decades of experience and “has been instrumental in developing successful key account and channel strategies, scalable go-to-market models and effective initiatives that build stronger customer and partner relationships,” according to the IQSIGHT announcement.

He has “a proven ability to lead high-performing teams, deliver consistent results and expand market presence,” the announcement says.

“IQSIGHT’s core strengths in visual intelligence and delivering high-quality, reliable solutions create an excellent foundation for growth,” says Wilkinson in the company announcement. “I look forward to working with the passionate and committed team in North America to deliver an exceptional customer experience providing technologies that help organizations reduce risk, improve safety and keep operations running smoothly.”

# World Fire Congress Advances Global Fire Service Collaboration

NFPA and IAFC to support WFC Secretariat function; UL Research Institutes to provide learning, research and global insight efforts.

Published: June 11, 2026SSI Staff

\[display\_gallery\_copyright\_text\]

![Featured Image](<Base64-Image-Removed>)

Logo courtesy of World Fire Congress

**MEDINA, Ohio —** The [World Fire Congress (WFC)](https://web.cvent.com/event/2bf92c0f-ded1-47c8-82ab-fd75bca10225/websitePage:fdba6cb2-b4f4-43c6-a9d6-433567710f7c) has named the Metropolitan Fire Chiefs Association (Metro Chiefs), a section of the [National Fire Protection Association](https://www.securitysales.com/tag/nationalfireprotectionassociation/) ( [NFPA](https://www.securitysales.com/tag/nfpa/)) and the International Association of Fire Chiefs (IAFC), to serve as its Secretariat, according to an association announcement.

The decision “establish\[es\] a long-term coordination and continuity framework designed to strengthen global collaboration across the fire and emergency services profession,” the announcement says.

The Secretariat structure “will provide continuity between Congresses, preserve institutional knowledge, support host-nation coordination and strengthen sustained international engagement on emerging fire and life safety challenges,” according to the association announcement.

“It is an honor for the Metropolitan Fire Chiefs Association to serve as the Secretariat for the World Fire Congress,” says Otto Drozd III, executive secretary of Metro Chiefs, in the announcement. “What is being established through this partnership is far more than operational coordination for a single event.

![SSI Newsletter](<Base64-Image-Removed>)

“It is the long-term infrastructure designed to support continuity, global engagement and sustained collaboration for future Congresses and the international fire and emergency services community. With the support of NFPA and IAFC, combined with the research and learning efforts being advanced through UL Research Institutes’ Fire Safety Research Institute, the World Fire Congress is building a strong and enduring foundation capable of supporting global cooperation for generations to come,” he says.

## What is the World Fire Congress?

The World Fire Congress is a biennial global forum that “brings together fire and emergency service leaders to strengthen international cooperation, share knowledge and advance evidence-informed dialogue on evolving fire and life safety challenges impacting communities worldwide,” according to the announcement.

Topics include firefighter health and safety, climate-driven disasters, structural fires, wildfires, emerging technologies, prevention, response, recovery and resilience.

The 2026 World Fire Congress will take place Sept. 8-9 at the QEII Conference Centre in Westminster, London, hosted by the United Kingdom and organized by the National Fire Chiefs Council (NFCC).

In addition to the Secretariat announcement, the World Fire Congress confirmed that UL Research Institutes’ Fire Safety Research Institute (ULRI) “will support the Congress’ learning, research and insight efforts by developing global Communities of Practice designed to sustain collaboration between Congresses,” the announcement says.

Dubai, United Arab Emirates is scheduled to host the Congress in 2028, and proposals are currently being accepted for prospective host nations for 2030.

# Lessing Gold, Partner, Mitchell Silberberg & Knupp: Best Advice

Gold reveals the best advice he's ever gotten, gives pointers to security industry pros on the rise and names an inspiration for the sector.

Published: June 11, 2026SSI Staff

\[display\_gallery\_copyright\_text\]

![Gold Security Industry](<Base64-Image-Removed>)

Adobe Stock image by dalkosaminrah

Our Best Advice Q&A series reaches triple digits today and there’s no one more worthy of being the 100th person to participate than 2004 _SSI_ Industry Hall of Fame inductee Lessing Gold, [partner](https://www.msk.com/attorneys) at Mitchell Silberberg & Knupp. He shares the best advice he’s ever heard, gives tips to security industry newcomers and names a person to whom all others in the sector should always listen.

## **_Security Sales & Integration:_ What’s the best piece of advice you’ve ever received?**

**Lessing Gold:** Retain your sense of humor.

## **_SSI:_ What advice would you give to those looking to achieve success in the security industry?**

**Gold:** Always tell the truth and be honest and straightforward with your customers and your suppliers. If a job is beyond the scope of your ability or knowledge, don\`t accept it.

## **_SSI:_ If you could point to one person in the security industry and tell up-and-comers, “Make sure to listen to what they have to say,” whom would you pick and why?**

**Gold:** Peter Raymond. He knows the industry inside and out. He takes pride in what he does and is always ready to share his knowledge with new and upcoming men and women entering the industry. If he tells you something, listen!

# Why Early Access Planning Is Now Mission-Critical at Data Centers

Physical security and access control are no longer considerations that can be finalized late in the data center design process.

Published: June 10, 2026Brian Parrish

\[display\_gallery\_copyright\_text\]

![Data Center Security](<Base64-Image-Removed>)

Adobe Stock image by .shock

The rapid expansion of hyperscale and [colocation data centers](https://us.allegion.com/en/solutions/by-market/data-centers.html) is reshaping how project teams think about speed, scale and risk.

As demand climbs, so does the pressure to deliver facilities faster, often across multiple regions simultaneously. For security system integrators and consultants, this shift brings both opportunity and challenge.

Physical security and access control are no longer considerations that can be finalized late in the design process. Instead, they must be embedded early and approached as integral components of the overall delivery strategy.

At the center of this evolution is a simple reality: in mission-critical environments, delays are costly, and inconsistency introduces risk. The way doors, frames, hardware and access control systems are designed, specified and coordinated can have a measurable impact on project timelines, commissioning and long-term operations.

![SSI Newsletter](<Base64-Image-Removed>)

## **The Shift Toward Early-Stage Security Integration**

Traditionally, access control and door hardware are addressed after core architectural and engineering decisions are already in place. In many commercial applications, sequencing may still work. In hyperscale and colocation data centers, however, this reactive approach often leads to inefficiencies.

Late-stage coordination frequently results in:

- Increased RFIs as discrepancies emerge between drawings and real-world conditions
- Change orders driven by incompatibility between hardware and access control systems
- Rework that disrupts already compressed construction schedules

For integrators and consultants, this reactive model creates unnecessary complexity and limits the ability to influence outcomes.

Forward-thinking data center owners and operators are taking a different approach. They are bringing security consultants, door hardware experts and access control integrators into the conversation much earlier, often during schematic design or design development phases.

This shift allows project teams to establish clarity around system requirements, performance expectations and installation constraints before they become problems in the field.

## **Standardization as a Tool for Speed and Scale**

One of the most significant trends in modern data center development is the move toward standardization. Hyperscale operators are deploying repeatable design models across regions to accelerate delivery and maintain consistency across their portfolios.

For security integrators and consultants, this creates a unique opportunity to contribute beyond individual projects. Instead of designing one-off solutions, teams can help develop standardized prototypes for door openings, access control configurations and hardware sets.

These prototypes serve several critical functions:

- Eliminate ambiguity during specification development
- Reduce variation across multiple sites
- Streamline coordination between trades
- Provide a tested baseline that can be adapted, rather than reinvented

When properly implemented, standardized opening designs can dramatically reduce the volume of RFIs and change orders, while also improving installation efficiency. This is particularly valuable in fast-track environments where construction sequencing leaves little room for error.

## **The Expanding Role of Digital Specification Tools**

As projects scale in complexity, digital tools are playing an increasingly important role in how specifications are developed and communicated. Platforms that support collaborative hardware specification and prototyping allow architects, consultants and integrators to work from a shared source of truth.

For integrators, this has several advantages:

- Improved visibility into door hardware and access control requirements
- Greater alignment with architectural intent
- More accurate system integration planning

Digital prototyping also enables project teams to validate decisions earlier. Instead of discovering conflicts in the field, teams can resolve them during the design phase, when changes are less costly and easier to implement.

The result is a more coordinated approach that bridges the gap between design and deployment.

## **Perimeter Security and Exterior Openings**

While much of the focus in data center security has traditionally centered on interior access control, there is increased attention being paid to perimeter security and exterior openings.

For integrators and consultants, this includes:

- Secure perimeter fencing and controlled gate access
- Exterior-rated hardware capable of withstanding environmental exposure
- Integration of access control systems with outdoor applications

These environments introduce additional challenges. Exposure to moisture, temperature fluctuations and corrosion can impact performance if products are not properly specified. At the same time, perimeter access points are often the first line of defense, making reliability and durability essential.

Selecting and integrating hardware designed for exterior conditions, such as solutions engineered specifically for outdoor use, can help mitigate these risks. Just as importantly, coordinating these elements early ensures that perimeter security systems align with overall site design and operational requirements.

## **Resilience Beyond the Data Hall**

Resilience is a defining characteristic of mission-critical facilities, but it extends beyond servers and power systems. Physical security infrastructure must also support uptime and continuity.

For integrators, this means considering:

- How access control systems perform during power disruptions
- The durability of door hardware in high-cycle environments
- The ability to maintain and service systems without disrupting operations

It also reinforces the importance of working with manufacturers and partners who can provide not only products, but also application expertise and long-term support.

A holistic approach to resilience considers the entire lifecycle, from design and installation through ongoing maintenance and upgrades.

## **Collaboration as a Competitive Advantage**

As data centers continue to scale, collaboration across disciplines is becoming a defining factor in project success. The intersection of architecture, engineering, construction, and security requires alignment that goes beyond traditional handoffs.

For security system integrators and consultants, this creates an opportunity to take on a more strategic role. By engaging earlier, contributing to standardized designs and leveraging collaborative tools, they can help drive outcomes that benefit the entire project team.

Ultimately, the question is no longer just how to secure a facility. It is how to do so in a way that supports speed, reduces risk, and enables repeatability at scale.

In mission-critical environments, those who can bridge the gap between design intent and operational reality will be best positioned to deliver value.

_Brian Parrish is director of mission-critical data center solutions at [Allegion.](https://www.securitysales.com/tag/allegion/)_

# ZeroEyes Partners with Academic Innovators to Help Universities

ZeroEyes-Academic Innovators referral program enhances security and emergency response capabilities of higher education systems.

Published: June 9, 2026SSI Staff

\[display\_gallery\_copyright\_text\]

![ZeroEyes Academic Innovators](<Base64-Image-Removed>)

Adobe Stock image by weerapat1003

**PHILADELPHIA —** Multi-analytics weapons detection and threat intelligence platform creator [ZeroEyes](https://www.securitysales.com/tag/zeroeyes/) today announces a new partnership with Academic Innovators, a [solutions provider](https://academicinnovators.com/about/) solving the programs, governance, and facilities challenges facing American higher education.

The alliance “enables the two companies to combine complementary strengths to help higher education institutions navigate both long-term transformation and immediate safety challenges through a referral program,” according to the joint announcement.

Academic Innovators’ multidisciplinary approach “brings together a network of partners and professionals across the higher education ecosystem, including edtech providers, legal experts, financial advisors, investment bankers and public policy specialists, to develop forward-looking solutions for evolving institutional needs,” the announcement says.

The industry insiders and strategic collaborators “help colleges and universities anticipate change, navigate complexity and proactively shape their future with confidence,” according to the joint announcement.

![SSI Newsletter](<Base64-Image-Removed>)

## Why is ZeroEyes Partnering with Academic Innovators?

By uniting a future-focused advisory approach with ZeroEyes’ advanced threat detection and real-time response capabilities, the collaboration “empowers institutions to better anticipate threats, enhance preparedness and respond with confidence in an increasingly complex environment,” according to the joint announcement.

“We are pleased to partner with ZeroEyes to provide integrated solutions that not only help higher education leaders navigate evolving operational and financial pressures but also enhance campus safety and resilience in an increasingly complex threat landscape,” says Dr. Brian C. Mitchell, managing principal and president of Academic Innovators and past president of Washington & Jefferson College and Bucknell University, in the announcement.

ZeroEyes delivers an integrated suite of artificial intelligence-powered analytics and security tools, including capabilities such as weapons detection, real-time threat geolocation and more, designed to enhance preparedness, accelerate threat identification and enable effective response.

It provides real-time, actionable intelligence on the illegal brandishing of weapons, such as guns and knives, in or near occupied spaces, alerting local staff and law enforcement with images and precise location data, often in a matter of seconds from the moment a gun is detected.

“By combining our proactive safety technology with Academic Innovators’ forward-looking, multidisciplinary expertise, we’re helping institutions respond to threats faster and plan more effectively for a safer, more resilient future,” says Mike Lahiff, CEO and co-founder of ZeroEyes. “We are proud to partner with them.”

The alliance enables the two companies to combine complementary strengths to help higher education institutions navigate both long-term transformation and immediate safety challenges through a referral program. Academic Innovators’ multidisciplinary approach brings together a network of partners and professionals across the higher education ecosystem, including edtech providers, legal experts, financial advisors, investment bankers and public policy specialists, to develop forward-looking solutions for evolving institutional needs.

The industry insiders and strategic collaborators help colleges and universities anticipate change, navigate complexity and proactively shape their future with confidence. By uniting a future-focused advisory approach with ZeroEyes’ advanced threat detection and real-time response capabilities, the collaboration empowers institutions to better anticipate threats, enhance preparedness and respond with confidence in an increasingly complex environment.

“We are pleased to partner with ZeroEyes to provide integrated solutions that not only help higher education leaders navigate evolving operational and financial pressures but also enhance campus safety and resilience in an increasingly complex threat landscape,” says Dr. Brian C. Mitchell, managing principal and president of Academic Innovators and past president of Washington & Jefferson College and Bucknell University.

ZeroEyes delivers an integrated suite of artificial intelligence-powered analytics and security tools, including capabilities such as weapons detection, real-time threat geolocation and more, designed to enhance preparedness, accelerate threat identification and enable effective response. It provides real-time, actionable intelligence on the illegal brandishing of weapons, such as guns and knives, in or near occupied spaces, alerting local staff and law enforcement with images and precise location data, often in a matter of seconds from the moment a gun is detected.

“By combining our proactive safety technology with Academic Innovators’ forward-looking, multidisciplinary expertise, we’re helping institutions respond to threats faster and plan more effectively for a safer, more resilient future,” says Mike Lahiff, CEO and co-founder of ZeroEyes. “We are proud to partner with them.”

# How Integrators Help Customers Go from Surveillance to Prevention

Advancements have created tremendous opportunities for security integrators to deliver smarter and more capable surveillance solutions.

Published: June 9, 2026Justin Gant

\[display\_gallery\_copyright\_text\]

![Surveillance](<Base64-Image-Removed>)

Adobe Stock image by as-artmedia

Security integrators have spent the last decade helping customers deploy increasingly sophisticated detection technologies. From artificial intelligence analytics and gun detection to license plate recognition, LiDAR and advanced video analytics, today’s security systems can [identify threats](https://www.securitysales.com/topic/surveillance/) faster and more accurately than ever.

These advancements have created tremendous opportunities for integrators to deliver smarter and more capable solutions. Yet as detection technology continues to evolve, many end users are asking their integrators a new question: “what happens after the alert?”

The reality is that detection alone does not stop incidents. Detection creates awareness but awareness without action often leaves organizations reacting to events rather than preventing them. As detection technologies continue to improve, security integrators are uniquely positioned to help customers build strategies that move beyond awareness and toward prevention.

## **The Shift from Surveillance to Prevention**

For many years, physical security systems were designed primarily for forensic purposes. Cameras captured footage, recordings were stored, and evidence could be reviewed after an incident occurred.

![SSI Newsletter](<Base64-Image-Removed>)

Today, many customers want more than evidence. They want solutions that can influence outcomes before an event escalates.

As a result, organizations are increasingly looking to their integrators for guidance on how to bridge the gap between detection and response. The conversation is no longer limited to whether a system can identify a threat. It now includes questions such as:

- How will the organization respond?
- Can intervention occur before a loss takes place?
- What technologies can help influence behavior?
- How can response workflows be automated or improved?

These questions are creating new opportunities for integrators to deliver greater value than ever before.

## **Building Response into Your Surveillance Strategy**

As customer expectations evolve, security integrators are helping organizations move beyond standalone devices and toward coordinated response strategies.

Examples include:

- Automated notifications and escalation paths
- Monitoring center integration
- Live voice communication
- Automated lighting and visual deterrence
- AI-assisted response workflows
- Multi-layered security ecosystems

Rather than relying on a single technology, many organizations are adopting layered security strategies that combine analytics, monitoring, deterrence, communications, and automation into a coordinated response framework.

The goal is no longer simply to know that something happened. The goal is to create a framework that helps reduce risk in real time.

For integrators, one emerging opportunity is the deployment of active deterrence units that combine surveillance, audio communication, and visual intervention into a single platform. These systems can often be layered onto existing camera infrastructure, allowing integrators to help customers improve response capabilities without requiring costly rip-and-replace projects.

This flexibility is particularly important as organizations seek to improve security outcomes while maximizing the value of their existing cameras, VMS platforms, and monitoring investments.

## **Designing Security Around Human Behavior**

One of the most important conversations taking place in the security industry today has less to do with technology and more to do with human behavior.

Technology plays a critical role in identifying threats, but security professionals are increasingly evaluating how individuals respond to communication, intervention, and deterrence.

Questions such as these are becoming more common:

- What causes an individual to abandon suspicious behavior?
- When is human intervention more effective than automation?
- How should responses escalate based on the severity of an event?
- Which actions produce the greatest impact in the shortest amount of time?

For integrators, these conversations represent an opportunity to move beyond equipment recommendations and become strategic advisors.

Customers are increasingly seeking guidance not only on what technologies to deploy, but also on how those technologies should work together to influence behavior, improve response times, and reduce risk.

The most successful security programs are not necessarily those with the most devices. They are often the programs designed around how people actually behave in real-world situations.

Increasingly, organizations are recognizing that the ultimate goal of security is not simply to document incidents after they occur. It is to prevent them from occurring in the first place.

## **A New Opportunity for Security Integrators**

As organizations shift from surveillance toward prevention, the role of the security integrator continues to expand.

Customers are no longer looking solely for hardware providers. They are looking for trusted advisors who can help them create safer environments, reduce risk, and improve operational outcomes.

This creates opportunities for integrators to deliver value in areas such as:

- Security workflow design
- Response planning
- Monitoring integrations
- Layered security strategies
- Deterrence technologies
- Risk reduction initiatives

By helping customers connect detection, response, and prevention into a cohesive strategy, integrators can differentiate themselves in an increasingly competitive market.

More importantly, they can help customers achieve the outcomes they care about most: fewer incidents, faster response times, and greater confidence in their security investments.

## **Looking Ahead**

The industry has made tremendous progress in its ability to detect threats.

Artificial intelligence will continue to improve. Analytics will become more accurate. Sensors will become more sophisticated. Detection capabilities will continue to expand.

The next phase of innovation, however, may be less about identifying threats and more about preventing incidents before they occur.

For years, security integrators helped customers answer the question: “Can we detect it?”

Increasingly, customers are asking a different question: “Can we prevent it?”

The integrators who can help bridge the gap between detection, response, and prevention will be best positioned to lead the next chapter of the physical security industry.

_Justin Gant is [chief executive officer and co-founder](https://action-cs.com/contact/) of Action-CS._

# SIA Welcomes New Chairman of Data Privacy Advisory Board

Tony Manna of Allegion will lead the SIA Data Privacy Advisory Board, an expert group of security industry privacy leaders.

Published: June 9, 2026SSI Staff

\[display\_gallery\_copyright\_text\]

![Data Privacy Manna](<Base64-Image-Removed>)

Image courtesy of Security Industry Association (SIA)

**SILVER SPRING, Md.—** The [Security Industry Association](https://www.securitysales.com/tag/securityindustryassociation/) ( [SIA](https://www.securitysales.com/tag/sia/)) has named Tony Manna as the new chairman of the SIA [Data Privacy Advisory Board](https://www.securityindustry.org/committee/data-privacy-advisory-board/), according to an association announcement.

The SIA Data Privacy Advisory Board “provides information and best practices to help SIA members handle sensitive data in a safe and secure manner to protect the personally identifiable information of their employees, partners and customers from potential abuses, breaches and misuses,” the announcement says.

Manna is associate general counsel and deputy chief privacy officer at global security products and solutions provider Allegion, which serves both residential and commercial markets in more than 120 countries. He advises senior leadership and business teams across a broad range of legal matters, supporting strategic initiatives and helping the organization navigate complex legal and regulatory issues.

Manna holds a bachelor’s degree, a Juris Doctor and a Master of Science in cybersecurity risk management from Indiana University. He is recognized as a Certified Information Privacy Professional/United States (CIPP/US) and Certified Information Privacy Manager (CIPM) by the International Association of Privacy Professionals.

![SSI Newsletter](<Base64-Image-Removed>)

## Why is Manna SIA Data Privacy Advisory Board Chairman?

Manna moderated an SIA Education@ISC conference session on data privacy at [ISC West 2026](https://www.securitysales.com/news/isc-west-2026-29k-attendance/618019/) and hosted a breakout room for the Data Privacy Advisory Board during the 2026 SIA Open House.

Key Data Privacy Advisory Board activities and accomplishments include:

- Developing the Security Cornerstones Learning Series module on data privacy,
- Publishing the SIA Privacy Code of Conduct and data privacy codes of practices for video surveillance and access control to guide the handling of sensitive data and
- Developing the Data Privacy Pro Certificate program, which helps security professionals advance their expertise on key data privacy concepts and gain strategies for data protection and compliance.

“I’m honored to serve as chair of the SIA Data Privacy Advisory Board and to build on the group’s strong foundation, including initiatives such as the SIA Data Privacy Pro Certificate,” says Manna in the SIA announcement.

Programs like this help security professionals understand evolving privacy and security challenges and apply that knowledge in practical, real-world scenarios to strengthen data protection,” he says. “As organizations navigate an increasingly complex mix of federal, state and global privacy requirements alongside rapid advances in artificial intelligence and shifting security standards, they need practical, experience-driven guidance. I look forward to working with the board to develop resources that help organizations manage risk, strengthen trust and protect the data entrusted to them.”

“SIA is proud to welcome Tony Manna as chair of the SIA Data Privacy Advisory Board,” says SIA CEO Don Erickson in the association announcement. “Tony’s deep knowledge of privacy, data protection and risk management and strong leadership experience will provide great value to the advisory board going forward.

“We look forward to working with Tony to build on the advisory board’s educational content, best practices resources and analysis of the complex privacy, legal and regulatory environment our industry must navigate,” he says.

# Freddy Kuo, Chairman, Luminys Systems Corp.: Best Advice

Kuo offers up the best advice he's heard, helps security industry pros on the rise and shines the spotlight on a highly important voice.

Published: June 9, 2026SSI Staff

\[display\_gallery\_copyright\_text\]

![Kuo Security Industry](<Base64-Image-Removed>)

Photo courtesy of Luminys

Our Best Advice Q&A series creeps closer to a major milestone with Freddy Kuo, [chairman](https://www.luminyscorp.com/about-us#we-are-luminys) of Luminys Systems Corp. and special office executive assistant at Foxlink. He shares the best advice he’s ever gotten, gives a tip to security industry newcomers and singles out the person to whom all others should always listen.

## **_Security Sales & Integration:_ What’s the best piece of advice you’ve ever received?**

**Freddy Kuo:** One of the best pieces of advice I’ve received is: “Listen to the problem before you present the solution.”

That has stayed with me because it is very easy in this industry to lead with technology. We all get excited about the newest capabilities, whether it’s better cameras, artificial intelligence analytics, cloud platforms or new integrations.

But, when you sit down with a customer or integrator, the conversation usually becomes more practical very quickly. They are trying to protect people, reduce risk, respond faster and make better decisions. If you start with the product before you understand that reality, you are already moving too fast.

![SSI Newsletter](<Base64-Image-Removed>)

That advice has shaped the way I look at product development and leadership. The best ideas come from understanding what integrators, dealers and end users actually experience in the field. If you understand the problem first, you can build something that is useful in the field, not just impressive in a demo.

## **_SSI:_ What advice would you give to those looking to achieve success in the security industry?**

**Kuo:** My biggest piece of advice is to learn how the entire security ecosystem works and spend time where the work actually happens.

Success in this industry requires more than knowing cameras, access control or AI. You need to understand how a manufacturer’s decision affects a distributor, how that affects an integrator and how all of it eventually affects the customer using the system every day.

Early in your career, spend time with installers and visit job sites. Talk to customers after deployment, not just during the sales process. Pay attention to what slows projects down, from installation time and network issues to user training, service calls, cybersecurity concerns and long-term support.

If you stay curious, keep learning and never lose touch with the realities customers face every day, you’ll make better decisions.

## **_SSI:_ If you could point to one person in the security industry and tell up-and-comers, “Make sure to listen to what they have to say,” whom would you pick and why?**

**Kuo:** I would point to Wayne Hurd, our VP of sales at Luminys. One thing people can learn from Wayne is the importance of staying close to the channel. He spends a lot of time listening to integrators, dealers and partners and he understands the pressure they carry when they recommend a system to a customer.

That has influenced how I think about this industry. A good security solution is shaped by more than what happens in a product meeting. It is shaped by the people who install it, sell it, support it and depend on it after deployment.

The broader lesson is that trust is built slowly. If you want people to believe in what you are building, you have to listen consistently, communicate clearly and understand what they are dealing with after the sale.”

Freddy Kuo, Chairman, Luminys Systems Corp.: Best Advice

Kuo offers up the best advice he's heard, helps security industry pros on the rise and shines the spotlight on a highly important voice.

Published: June 9, 2026SSI Staff

Our Best Advice Q&A series creeps closer to a major milestone with Freddy Kuo, chairman of Luminys Systems Corp. and special office executive assistant at Foxlink. He shares the best advice he’s ever gotten, gives a tip to security industry newcomers and singles out the person to whom all others should always listen.

Security Sales & Integration: What’s the best piece of advice you’ve ever received?

Freddy Kuo: One of the best pieces of advice I’ve received is: “Listen to the problem before you present the solution.”

That has stayed with me because it is very easy in this industry to lead with technology. We all get excited about the newest capabilities, whether it’s better cameras, artificial intelligence analytics, cloud platforms or new integrations.

But, when you sit down with a customer or integrator, the conversation usually becomes more practical very quickly. They are trying to protect people, reduce risk, respond faster and make better decisions. If you start with the product before you understand that reality, you are already moving too fast.

That advice has shaped the way I look at product development and leadership. The best ideas come from understanding what integrators, dealers and end users actually experience in the field. If you understand the problem first, you can build something that is useful in the field, not just impressive in a demo.

SSI: What advice would you give to those looking to achieve success in the security industry?

Kuo: My biggest piece of advice is to learn how the entire security ecosystem works and spend time where the work actually happens.

Success in this industry requires more than knowing cameras, access control or AI. You need to understand how a manufacturer’s decision affects a distributor, how that affects an integrator and how all of it eventually affects the customer using the system every day.

Early in your career, spend time with installers and visit job sites. Talk to customers after deployment, not just during the sales process. Pay attention to what slows projects down, from installation time and network issues to user training, service calls, cybersecurity concerns and long-term support.

If you stay curious, keep learning and never lose touch with the realities customers face every day, you’ll make better decisions.

SSI: If you could point to one person in the security industry and tell up-and-comers, “Make sure to listen to what they have to say,” whom would you pick and why?

Kuo: I would point to Wayne Hurd, our VP of sales at Luminys. One thing people can learn from Wayne is the importance of staying close to the channel. He spends a lot of time listening to integrators, dealers and partners and he understands the pressure they carry when they recommend a system to a customer.

That has influenced how I think about this industry. A good security solution is shaped by more than what happens in a product meeting. It is shaped by the people who install it, sell it, support it and depend on it after deployment.

The broader lesson is that trust is built slowly. If you want people to believe in what you are building, you have to listen consistently, communicate clearly and understand what they are dealing with after the sale.”

# Emergency24, Worldview Monitoring Ink Partnership

The partnership combines Emergency24's monitoring infrastructure and dealer network with Worldview Monitoring's experience in remote guarding.

Published: June 8, 2026SSI Staff

\[display\_gallery\_copyright\_text\]

![Emergency24 Worldview](<Base64-Image-Removed>)

Logo courtesy of Emergency24

**DES PLAINES, Ill.–** Third-party central station alarm monitoring company [Emergency24](https://www.securitysales.com/tag/emergency24/) has entered into a [strategic partnership](https://www.emergency24.us/our-partners/) with Worldview Monitoring focused on “supporting the growing demand for remote guarding services across the United States,” according to the joint announcement.

The partnership “combines Emergency24’s established monitoring infrastructure and dealer network with Worldview Monitoring’s experience in remote guarding delivery,” the announcement says.

Together, the companies “aim to help monitoring centers, dealers and security providers introduce and expand remote guarding services in a way that supports long-term growth, recurring revenue opportunities and operational consistency,” according to the joint announcement.

## Why Are Emergency24 & Worldview Monitoring Partnering?

The partnership between Emergency24 and Worldview Monitoring is “designed to address that need through a service model focused on operational consistency, structured escalation and helping dealers introduce remote guarding in a way that aligns with how they already support commercial customers,” the announcement says.

![SSI Newsletter](<Base64-Image-Removed>)

“Remote guarding has moved well beyond being a niche offering,” says Tim Pearman, CEO of Worldview Monitoring, in the joint announcement. “More dealers and monitoring organizations are actively evaluating how to support it, but maintaining consistency becomes increasingly important as deployments scale.”

“Our partnership with Emergency24 is significant because it validates the model within the U.S. market. The focus is not just on analytics or technology. It’s about delivering the service consistently and helping partners introduce remote guarding in a way that aligns with how they already operate,” he says.

Emergency24 “views the partnership as part of a broader shift taking place across the security industry as video monitoring continues evolving into a more proactive service category,” according to the joint announcement.

“Commercial customers are asking dealers more questions about remote guarding because they want greater visibility and faster intervention when activity occurs after hours,” says Steve Mayer, CEO of Emergency24, in the announcement. “For many dealers, the opportunity now is figuring out how to introduce those services in a way that supports long-term growth while remaining manageable operationally as accounts expand.

“Worldview’s experience in remote guarding delivery made this a strong fit for us. The partnership gives our dealers access to a proven operational model while maintaining the consistency and reliability they expect from Emergency24,” he says.

The partnership “will support monitoring centers, dealers and security providers looking to introduce remote guarding through a structure designed to integrate with existing monitoring environments, dealer workflows and customer relationships,” according to the joint announcement.

# Commercial Security Made Easy with Wireless Locks from ProdataKey (PDK)

The Red™ Wireless Cylindrical Lock from ProdataKey represents an intuitive approach to commercial security by delivering easy installation, flexible management, and reliable cloud connectivity.

Published: June 8, 2026ProdataKey

\[display\_gallery\_copyright\_text\]

![Featured Image](<Base64-Image-Removed>)

Adobe Stock image by Zhu Difeng, Product Image from ProdataKey

As demands for smarter, scalable commercial security solutions continue to grow, ProdataKey ( [PDK](https://www.prodatakey.com/)) has expanded its portfolio with the introduction of the [award-winning](https://www.prodatakey.com/single-post/pdk-red-wireless-locksets-win-ssi-mvp-award) [Red™ Wireless Cylindrical Lock](https://www.prodatakey.com/red-wireless-locksets/cylindrical). Meticulously designed for commercial applications of any size, the Red Cylindrical Lock delivers a streamlined approach to access control that prioritizes ease of use, cost effectiveness, and longevity.

### What are the Security Needs of Today’s Commercial Spaces?

From [office buildings](https://www.prodatakey.com/single-post/freedom-business-collective-case-study) and [educational institutions](https://www.prodatakey.com/single-post/the-peak-in-academics-and-security) to [healthcare facilities](https://www.prodatakey.com/single-post/how-pdk-protects-a-large-scale-healthcare-facility-case-study) and [multi-site enterprises](https://www.prodatakey.com/single-post/idahoan-case-study), commercial organizations must balance security, convenience, and operational efficiency. Traditional mechanical locks often lack the flexibility required for modern environments, while hardwired access control solutions can be costly and time-consuming to install. At the same time, facility managers are seeking systems that support [remote management](https://www.prodatakey.com/software), real-time visibility, and seamless scalability. As businesses grow and security requirements evolve, access control solutions must be able to adapt without creating additional complexity or excessive infrastructure costs.

[Cloud-based security](https://www.prodatakey.com/single-post/2018/10/18/safely-invisible-the-powerful-security-of-cloud-based-access-control) technologies have emerged as a preferred approach, enabling organizations to manage credentials, monitor activity, and make security updates from virtually anywhere. The result is a more responsive and efficient security strategy that aligns with the needs of today’s connected workplaces.

### What Sets the Red Wireless Cylindrical Lock Apart?

The [Red Wireless Cylindrical Lock](https://www.prodatakey.com/red-wireless-locksets/cylindrical) was developed to address these modern security challenges with a streamlined and user-friendly approach. Designed for [commercial applications](https://www.prodatakey.com/industry/commercial-real-estate) of any size, the lock combines advanced access control capabilities with simplified deployment and management.

![SSI Newsletter](<Base64-Image-Removed>)

One of its most significant advantages is ease of installation. Because the lock communicates wirelessly, organizations can avoid the expense and disruption often associated with running new wiring to doors. This allows facilities to expand access control coverage more quickly and cost-effectively. The solution also provides flexible management through PDK’s cloud-based platform, [PDK.io](http://pdk.io/)—giving administrators the ability to manage access permissions, monitor activity, and make updates remotely. This flexibility helps organizations maintain security while reducing administrative burden.

The Red Cylindrical Lock from ProdataKey represents an intuitive approach to commercial security by delivering easy installation, flexible management, and reliable cloud connectivity. To learn more about how the Red Cylindrical Lock meets the needs of modern commercial environments, visit [prodatakey.com/red-wireless-locksets](http://prodatakey.com/red-wireless-locksets) or reach out to [sales@prodatakey.com](mailto:sales@prodatakey.com). # Pye-Barker Acquires Washington-Based Fire Protection Specialists

Fire Protection Specialists will add integrated fire protection services to Pye-Barker's existing fire alarm and security offerings.

Published: June 8, 2026SSI Staff

\[display\_gallery\_copyright\_text\]

![Pye-Barker Fire Protection Specialists, Pye-Barker AAA, Pye-Barker Priority One Security, Pye-Barker Philadelphia Detection Systems](<Base64-Image-Removed>)

Logo courtesy of Pye-Barker Fire & Safety

- _Pye-Barker Fire & Safety has acquired Fire Protection Specialists of Liberty Lake, Wash._
- _The deal will add integrated fire protection services to Pye-Barker’s existing fire alarm and security offerings in the Pacific Northwest_
- _Fire Protection Specialists serves Washington, Oregon, Idaho, Montana and California with advanced system monitoring, system inspections and testing and fire extinguisher service._

**ATLANTA —** Full-service fire protection, life safety and service service provider [Pye-Barker Fire & Safety](https://www.securitysales.com/tag/pye-barker-fire-safety/) has [acquired](https://pyebarkerfs.com/acquisitions/) Liberty Lake, Wash.-based Fire Protection Specialists, strengthening “its comprehensive services for customers in the Northwest,” according to the joint announcement.

This transaction “will add integrated fire protection services to Pye-Barker’s existing fire alarm and security offerings in the Pacific Northwest,” the announcement says.

Established in 1999, Fire Protection Specialists serves Washington, Oregon, Idaho, Montana and California with the installation and servicing of fire suppression and fire alarm systems for commercial and industrial customers, including education, utility, government and healthcare facilities.

The company’s fire protection solutions include advanced system monitoring, system inspections and testing and fire extinguisher service.

![SSI Newsletter](<Base64-Image-Removed>)

## Why Did Pye-Barker Acquire Fire Protection Specialists?

Fire Protection Specialists offers clean agent fire suppression systems to extinguish fire in high value spaces, such as data centers, equipment vaults and MRI/CAT scan rooms. The team also has expertise in automatic extinguishing systems for commercial kitchens and off-road fire suppression systems for heavy mobile equipment.

“We welcome the Fire Protection Specialists team to the Pye-Barker family with open arms,” says Bart Proctor, CEO of Pye-Barker, in the joint announcement. “They have a longstanding reputation of expert care in their community, and that legacy was clear in every conversation we had with their team.

“As we join forces, I’m excited for us to strengthen our customer service in Washington and beyond,” he says.

Fire Protection Specialists’ technicians and staff will continue to serve customers in the Northwest. Nelson Mullins Riley & Scarborough, LLP represented Pye-Barker in the transaction.

Pye-Barker Acquires Washington-Based Fire Protection Specialists

Fire Protection Specialists will add integrated fire protection services to Pye-Barker's existing fire alarm and security offerings.

Published: June 8, 2026SSI Staff

Pye-Barker Fire & Safety has acquired Fire Protection Specialists of Liberty Lake, Wash. The deal will add integrated fire protection services to Pye-Barker’s existing fire alarm and security offerings in the Pacific Northwest Fire Protection Specialists serves Washington, Oregon, Idaho, Montana and California with advanced system monitoring, system inspections and testing and fire extinguisher service.

ATLANTA — Full-service fire protection, life safety and service service provider Pye-Barker Fire & Safety has acquired Liberty Lake, Wash.-based Fire Protection Specialists, strengthening “its comprehensive services for customers in the Northwest,” according to the joint announcement.

This transaction “will add integrated fire protection services to Pye-Barker’s existing fire alarm and security offerings in the Pacific Northwest,” the announcement says.

Established in 1999, Fire Protection Specialists serves Washington, Oregon, Idaho, Montana and California with the installation and servicing of fire suppression and fire alarm systems for commercial and industrial customers, including education, utility, government and healthcare facilities.

The company’s fire protection solutions include advanced system monitoring, system inspections and testing and fire extinguisher service.

Why Did Pye-Barker Acquire Fire Protection Specialists?

Fire Protection Specialists offers clean agent fire suppression systems to extinguish fire in high value spaces, such as data centers, equipment vaults and MRI/CAT scan rooms. The team also has expertise in automatic extinguishing systems for commercial kitchens and off-road fire suppression systems for heavy mobile equipment.

“We welcome the Fire Protection Specialists team to the Pye-Barker family with open arms,” says Bart Proctor, CEO of Pye-Barker, in the joint announcement. “They have a longstanding reputation of expert care in their community, and that legacy was clear in every conversation we had with their team.

“As we join forces, I’m excited for us to strengthen our customer service in Washington and beyond,” he says.

Fire Protection Specialists’ technicians and staff will continue to serve customers in the Northwest. Nelson Mullins Riley & Scarborough, LLP represented Pye-Barker in the transaction.
