# Integrators Need to Rethink Their Approach to School Security

The discussion about school security is no longer just about cameras, access control systems and emergency response protocols.

Published: June 8, 2026Dmitry Sokolowski

\[display\_gallery\_copyright\_text\]

![School Security](<Base64-Image-Removed>)

Adobe Stock image by alswart

Many schools use the summer months to plan for the next academic year, evaluating everything from safety upgrades and infrastructure investments to staffing, budgets and new technology deployments.

One of the most important conversations districts are having right now is around campus safety and security and what it should look like in 2026 and the next academic year. The discussion is no longer just about cameras, access control systems and emergency response protocols.

Schools are also trying to address fights, vandalism, student well-being, unauthorized visitors, behavioral warning signs and growing parent pressure to identify threats before they escalate.

This shift is changing the role security systems integrators are expected to play. Schools are looking beyond hardware and evaluating whether their overall security strategy can help staff identify risk earlier, improve visibility across campus operations and respond faster and smarter to potential incidents.

![SSI Newsletter](<Base64-Image-Removed>)

The good news is that most districts are not starting from scratch. According to the National Center for Education Statistics, nearly 93% of public schools already use security cameras in some capacity. In many cases, they already have extensive infrastructure installed across campuses, sometimes hundreds or thousands of cameras, access control systems and emergency communication tools.

The challenge is: much of this infrastructure still operates reactively, not proactively.

Security teams often need to manually review footage after incidents occur, piece together information across disconnected systems, or rely on staff members to recognize warning signs in real time while managing dozens of other responsibilities. The time and resources behind this add up.

The problem is not visibility. The problem is operational bandwidth.

A district may have hundreds or even thousands of cameras deployed across its campuses, but no school can realistically staff enough people to monitor every feed at all times. As campuses grow larger and schools struggle to staff security teams, many districts are realizing that adding more hardware alone does not necessarily improve situational awareness.

## **AI Changing What Schools Expect From Security**

Artificial intelligence is becoming a larger part of school security conversations and changing what districts expect from their technology partners and integrators. The conversation is becoming less about individual devices and more about how schools actually detect, communicate and respond to potential issues across campus.

For integrators, that changes the discussion entirely. Schools are increasingly asking operational questions like:

- Can technology help identify unusual activity earlier?
- Who receives alerts, and how are they prioritized?
- Can it improve coordination between administrators, school resource officers and security personnel?
- How do these teams respond?
- Can these systems realistically fit into existing workflows?

The answers matter because AI is only valuable if schools can operationalize it effectively. Technology should help staff process information faster and identify patterns that might otherwise go unnoticed, not overwhelm teams with additional complexity or constant false alarms.

Now, districts and decision committees are evaluating how well technology supports the people responsible for keeping campuses safe. Using AI to improve campus safety and security is ultimately a risk management decision, not a technology decision.

## **Integrators Risk Falling Behind As Schools Move Beyond Hardware**

Following major incidents on school campuses over the past several years, many districts invested heavily in emergency response planning and physical security measures. Those investments remain important, but administrators increasingly recognize that many safety incidents are preceded by observable warning signs.

In many cases, staff do not become aware of those situations until students, teachers or administrators report them after the fact. By then, the opportunity for early intervention may be limited and the situation may have already escalated.

As a result, schools are no longer evaluating security systems based solely on cameras, coverage areas or recording capabilities. They are looking for solutions that can help staff identify concerning activity earlier and respond more effectively.

That shift is changing what districts expect from integrators. School leaders want strategic partners who understand deployment, alert management, staffing limitations and how new technologies fit into daily operations — not simply vendors focused on the next hardware upgrade.

## **Trust and Transparency Matter More Than Ever**

One of the biggest mistakes integrators can make right now is overselling what AI can realistically do in a school environment. Administrators are becoming far more educated buyers. They understand that no technology can predict every incident or replace human judgment.

They are looking for tools that improve visibility, reduce blind spots and help staff make faster, more informed decisions without overwhelming teams with false alarms.

Concerns around privacy, false positives and operational transparency are legitimate, particularly in sensitive environments involving students. Integrators who acknowledge those concerns directly and explain how systems are designed to support human decision-making, rather than replace it, are far more likely to build trust with district stakeholders.

The sales process itself is also becoming more complex. Conversations now involve superintendents, operations leaders, school boards and even parents, not just facilities or IT departments. That’s because security decisions are tied more closely to discussions around student well-being, campus culture and community trust.

## **The Future of School Security Will Favor Strategic Integrators**

As districts prepare for the next school year, it’s clear that modern school security is no longer just about documenting incidents after they happen. It is about improving awareness early enough to support prevention whenever possible.

The schools evaluating safety upgrades this summer are asking what technology can help them understand, prioritize and respond more effectively across increasingly complex campus environments.

Integrators who can help answer those questions thoughtfully, realistically and strategically will be far better positioned than those still approaching school security as a purely reactive, hardware-driven conversation.

The industry spent years solving visibility. The next decade will be about interpretation — turning information into action before incidents escalate.

# FieldResolve Expands Knowledge Base to 40,000+ Documents

Projects built inside FieldResolve can now encompass virtually any security or fire product an integrator or dealer.

Published: June 5, 2026SSI Staff

\[display\_gallery\_copyright\_text\]

![FieldResovle](<Base64-Image-Removed>)

Image courtesy of The CMOOR Group

**LOUISVILLE, Ky. —** The CMOOR Group, which [focuses](https://www.securitysales.com/tag/cmoorgroup/) on eLearning and compliance solutions for the physical security, fire protection and life safety industries, recently announced its artificial intelligence-powered [field support platform](https://www.fieldresolve.com/#why-field-resolve), FieldResolve, now houses more than 40,000 documents from 36 manufacturers.

This milestone makes FieldResolve “the most comprehensive technical knowledge base available to security and fire professionals,” according to the CMOOR Group announcement.

With this expansion, projects built inside FieldResolve “can now encompass virtually any security or fire product an integrator or dealer works with, from access control panels and intrusion detection systems to fire alarm controllers, video surveillance equipment and beyond,” the announcement says.

Technicians “can mirror the full, multi-manufacturer complexity of a real installation and get fast, accurate answers across every product on that job,” according to the company announcement.

![SSI Newsletter](<Base64-Image-Removed>)

## **How Does FieldResolve Help Integrators in the Field?**

“Real-world security integration is never single-manufacturer,” says Connie Moorhead, CEO and founder of The CMOOR Group, in the company announcement. “A field technician walks into a job and faces Johnson Controls panels, Bosch detectors, Avigilon cameras and Kidde Commercial fire systems, all in the same building. FieldResolve was built for that reality.”

“Multi-manufacturer environments are the norm, and among the most challenging scenarios a security technician can face,” according to the company announcement. “When a system fault occurs, determining whether the problem originates with the panel, a device, the wiring or an integration between two different manufacturers requires deep cross-product troubleshooting knowledge that most technicians carry only through years of experience.

“FieldResolve changes that equation. The platform’s technical knowledge base spans products from Honeywell, Bosch, DMP and dozens of additional manufacturers, giving security and fire technicians a single resource that reflects the full scope of what they actually install,” the announcement says.

“By creating a project in FieldResolve that mirrors an actual installation, including all manufacturers present on the job, technicians can ask questions in plain language and receive precise, sourced answers drawn from that knowledge base,” according to the company announcement.

“For security and fire integrators managing large, complex installations, including schools, hospitals, high-rise buildings or enterprise campuses, the ability to perform multi-manufacturer troubleshooting from a single platform represents a significant operational advantage,” the announcement says. “Shorter service call resolution times protect both the customer relationship and the company’s bottom line.”

## **How Does FieldResolve Handle Data?**

FieldResolve is “also differentiated by how it handles data,” according to the company announcement. All queries and results are end-to-end encrypted, meaning “none of its data ever feeds into the broader large language model (LLM).”

“Information entered into FieldResolve remains secure and will never find its way to the internet at large, making it one of the few AI field technician support platforms built with enterprise-grade data privacy at its core,” the announcement says.

The 40,000-document, 36-manufacturer milestone “reflects The CMOOR Group’s ongoing commitment to building FieldResolve as a true field-ready platform, not a document search tool, but an intelligent technical partner that understands the life safety systems professionals install and service every day,” according to the company announcement.

# Rescuers Save 8 in Flooded Cave: Surveillance Videos of the Week

Other top surveillance videos this week include sonic booms and meteor explosions across the U.S., a deadly paper mill explosion and more.

Published: June 5, 2026D. Craig MacCormack

[View Gallery](https://www.securitysales.com/news/rescuers-save-8-flooded-cave-surveillance-videos-week/619227/slideshow/0)

Eight cave explorers looking for gold in Laos [had to be rescued](https://www.nbcnews.com/world/asia/laos-cave-survivor-gold-miners-trapped-cave-cramped-flooded-rcna348421) when the narrow path they were traveling got flooded. That harrowing mission was captured on surveillance video, making it the lead story in the latest edition of Surveillance Videos of the Week.

Other clips this week explore a recent trend by so-called “treasure hunters” in Brooklyn and Queens who were spotted climbing out of sewers in those boroughs, a deadly explosion at a paper mill in Washington that killed 11 people and a fireworks factory explosion in Malta.

One of the biggest stories of the week across the U.S. was the series of sonic booms, meteor explosions and fireballs. As you might imagine, those rare occurrences made for some spectacular videos!

# The Monitoring Association Elects 2026-2028 Board of Directors

The Monitoring Association (TMA) board members bring expertise from across the professional monitoring, security and technology sectors.

Published: June 5, 2026SSI Staff

\[display\_gallery\_copyright\_text\]

![TMA Board, ECCs, TMA Mid-Year Meeting](<Base64-Image-Removed>)

Logo courtesy of The Monitoring Association (TMA)

**McLEAN, Va. —** [The Monitoring Association](https://www.securitysales.com/tag/themonitoringassociation/) ( [TMA](https://www.securitysales.com/tag/tma/)) today announces the election of seven industry leaders to serve on its [board of directors](https://tma.us/about/our-leadership/) for the 2026–2028 term.

The directors will begin their terms following the association’s Annual Meeting in November 2026.

The following individuals were re-elected to the TMA board of directors:

- Michael Picciola, ADT, LLC – Vice President
- Justin Bailey, Becklar Monitoring – Secretary
- David Charney, Everon – At-Large Board Member
- Richard Flores, Puget Sound Energy – GSOC Board Member
- Brandon Niles, Acadian Monitoring Services, LLC – Contract Monitoring Board Member
- Joseph Pereira, Securitas Technology – At-Large Board Member
- Joey Rao-Russell, Kimberlite Corporation dba Sonitrol – Regional Board Member

## What Does TMA Leadership Say About the Board?

“TMA is fortunate to benefit from the expertise, vision, and commitment of these accomplished industry leaders,” says TMA president Alan Gillmore IV in the association announcement. “Their collective experience in professional monitoring, security and technology will help guide the association as it advances initiatives that strengthen the professional monitoring industry and support our members.”

![SSI Newsletter](<Base64-Image-Removed>)

As members of the board of directors, the elected leaders “will help shape the association’s strategic direction and oversee programs that advance public safety, industry standards, education, advocacy and innovation throughout the monitoring and security sectors,” according to the TMA announcement.

# SIA Appoints Jasvir Gill as Vice Chairman of Utilities Advisory Board

Gill will join SIA Utilities Advisory Board chairman Joey St. Jacques in leading the expert group of utility security thought leaders.

Published: June 4, 2026SSI Staff

\[display\_gallery\_copyright\_text\]

![Gill Utilities](<Base64-Image-Removed>)

Image courtesy of Security Industry Association (SIA)

**SILVER SPRING, Md.—** The [Security Industry Association](https://www.securitysales.com/tag/securityindustryassociation/) ( [SIA](https://www.securitysales.com/tag/sia/)) has named Dr. Jasvir Gill as the new vice chairman of the [SIA Utilities Advisory Board](https://www.securityindustry.org/committee/utilities-advisory-board/), which “demonstrates thought leadership on compliance and technology topics of interest to professionals managing security at utility facilities.”

Gill is founder and CEO of Alert Enterprise and he has spent more than two decades advancing enterprise security through artificial intelligence-driven automation and identity-first security strategies. In recognition of his contributions to engineering, technology and industry leadership, Gill was awarded an honorary doctorate of engineering by Guru Nanak Dev University in 2026.

Prior to founding Alert Enterprise, he founded Virsa Systems, a governance, risk and compliance and application security company acquired by SAP in 2006. Beyond business, Gill supports industry and community initiatives, including serving on advisory boards and leading Trakki, his initiative focused on education, AI learning and community development in Punjab, India.

## Why is Jasvir Gill the Vice Chairman of the SIA UAB?

When the SIA Utilities Advisory Board was established in 2022, Gill was among the group’s founding members and immediately stepped into the role of Technology Subcommittee chairman. He has been “engaged with the advisory board’s development of educational content to help utility security practitioners, integrators and end users tackle cyber-physical convergence in practical, actionable terms,” according to the SIA announcement.

![SSI Newsletter](<Base64-Image-Removed>)

“Critical infrastructure is the backbone of modern society, and securing it is one of the defining challenges of our time. I am honored to serve as vice chair of the SIA Utilities Advisory Board and collaborate with some of the brightest minds in our industry to advance the future of cyber-physical security,” says Gill in the announcement.

“We have an extraordinary opportunity to reimagine security as a catalyst for resilience, operational excellence and sustainable growth,” he says. “By bringing together innovation, leadership and a shared commitment to protecting what matters most, we can help build a safer, stronger and more connected world.”

## What’s the SIA Reaction to the New UAB Vice Chairman?

“SIA is proud to welcome Dr. Jasvir Gill as vice chair of the SIA Utilities Advisory Board,” says SIA CEO Don Erickson in the association announcement. “Since this group was established, Jasvir has brought his conviction, passion and expertise to helping address the unique security challenges facing utilities.

“His leadership in partnership with chair Joey St. Jacques will be immensely valuable in the advisory board’s efforts to shape how the next generation of security professionals approaches the protection of critical infrastructure,” says Erickson.

The SIA Utilities Advisory Board develops recommendations and guidance for the physical security and cybersecurity of utilities infrastructure, offers formal responses to security rules and guidance proposed by regulatory agencies, shares knowledge with related industries and develops content for SIA events and publications.

Key advisory board initiatives include helping to develop the Security Cornerstones module on critical infrastructure security, hosting the annual Protecting Utilities lunch events at ISC West and East, developing a six-session SIAacademy LIVE! course on securing utilities and the energy sector and developing SIA’s Guide to NERC CIP Compliance.

# How to Find Integration Partners Who Will Drive Long-Term Growth

Due diligence with integration partners can catalyze your growth through marketing streams, increased market exposure and proven excellence.

Published: June 4, 2026Celeste Miller

\[display\_gallery\_copyright\_text\]

![Integration Partners](<Base64-Image-Removed>)

Adobe Stock image by ASDF

Security integrators often invest significant effort engaging with technology providers or manufacturers that fail to deliver what customers actually need. In the worst cases, so-called “partners” actively hurt the integrator’s business or deliver short-sighted solutions that don’t contribute to an optimal security posture.

The good news is that great partnerships are possible — and due diligence in partnership coordination can catalyze your growth through new marketing streams, increased market exposure and proven excellence in your craft.

To help you avoid poor partnerships and effectively deliver on your customers’ needs, let’s explore the realities of partner development today, red flags you should look for, and proven ways to transform your partner strategy into a long-term growth advantage.

## What’s a Successful Provider-Integrator Relationship?

Customers increasingly need integrators to bring more than piecemeal solutions to the table. The security market is flooded with vendors and focused capabilities, but every investment must support a holistic, programmatic solution that efficiently meets the stated goals.

![SSI Newsletter](<Base64-Image-Removed>)

Some solution providers may appear to be a perfect fit for your customers’ current need, however, these relationships can quickly introduce reputational risk or simply be unable to generate ongoing customer value.

The most effective partnerships are built on the following elements:

- **Established rules of engagement.** Vendors should not compete with you for business. Friction is inevitable when there’s no alignment between the vendor’s partner program and overall go-to-market strategy. Develop an agreed upon rules of engagement with every partner to clarify how each of you will operate, what responsibilities you hold and how you can benefit each other’s growth. Each partner should understand how they will invest in scoping the right program for the needs of the end customer.

- **Joint sales motions.** It’s unrealistic (and unsustainable) to expect your team to be experts in every security sector and solution provider. Effective partners enable your sales team with resources and education that make it easy to identify when that partner may be the right fit for a customer and how to bring them into the conversation.

- **Long-term commitment.** Vendors focus solely on an initial sale and then remove themselves from ongoing conversations. As your customers’ needs continue to change, actual partners are prepared and eager to consider alternate implementations or strategies that reflect the newest needs and opportunities.

- **Open collaboration with industry players.** Your chosen partners need to understand and appreciate the entire ecosystem your business operates with. Individual vendors aren’t the only players in their space, and the best partners will collaborate with other vendors in your network and invest resources to ensure complete cohesion across every solution you deploy for customers.


These guiding principles will help you define what you are seeking in prospective partners. Next is strengthening your ability to evaluate partners for alignment with those principles.

## How to Assess Integration Partners for Long-Term Value

Thorough vetting of any potential partner can reduce the risk of false starts or building a network of frenemies who don’t have your best interest in mind.

There are several red flags to look for when deciding whether a vendor is trustworthy to partner with, exemplifies a commitment to preserving your customer experience, and will ultimately support your brand’s reputation and growth.

Ask questions like these throughout your discovery and evaluation process to develop the greatest likelihood of a fulfilling partnership:

- **“How does your direct sales program support partner relationships?”** Any partner should be able to clearly explain how they work with you and not directly compete with you. The most successful partnerships are built from a team selling approach where the integrator can benefit from the expertise and collaboration of the direct sales team.

- **“What joint marketing opportunities do you hope to engage in?”** Ideal partnerships uplift all parties in spaces where buyers engage: trade shows, exclusive events, webinars and content experiences delivered in online channels. Explore joint marketing options from the beginning to gain a solid understanding of how mature the partner’s marketing function is and whether they will bring as much to the table as you will.

- **“Do you have a tiered partner program, or how do you incentivize partners that bring more business to you?”** As your team generates business for vendors, you should understand how that investment is rewarded and if they prioritize organizations that deliver significant value.

- **“How quickly can you respond to support needs and how do you assist us with product or service concerns?”** The post-sale experience is just as crucial as implementation. Customers will call you when they encounter a problem and it is your reputation on the line if a partner’s solution causes an issue. Align with partners on how they partner with you to solve challenges and what support they do or do not provide.


## Partnerships Are Your Best Business Investment

A strategic partnership mindset delivers a win-win-win that creates a flywheel of success: happier customers who retain their business and recommend you to others, higher operational efficiency with greater flexibility to reach new buyers, and combined power with partners to engage buyers and stay ahead of market trends.

Achieving this reality starts one partner at a time, helping you better spot the vendors who are invested in your growth and eager to tackle your customer challenges together.

_Celeste Miller is [director of channels](https://www.lvt.com/story) for [LiveView Technologies](https://www.securitysales.com/tag/liveview-technologies/) ( [LVT](https://www.securitysales.com/tag/lvt/))._

Some solution providers may appear to be a perfect fit for your customers’ current need, however, these relationships can quickly introduce reputational risk or simply be unable to generate ongoing customer value.

The most effective partnerships are built on established rules of engagement, joint sales motions, long-term commitment, and open collaboration with industry players.

These guiding principles will help you define what you are seeking in prospective partners. Next is strengthening your ability to evaluate partners for alignment with those principles.

Thorough vetting of any potential partner can reduce the risk of false starts or building a network of frenemies who don’t have your best interest in mind.

There are several red flags to look for when deciding whether a vendor is trustworthy to partner with, exemplifies a commitment to preserving your customer experience, and will ultimately support your brand’s reputation and growth.

Ask questions like these throughout your discovery and evaluation process to develop the greatest likelihood of a fulfilling partnership:

- “How does your direct sales program support partner relationships?”
- “What joint marketing opportunities do you hope to engage in?”
- “Do you have a tiered partner program, or how do you incentivize partners that bring more business to you?”
- “How quickly can you respond to support needs and how do you assist us with product or service concerns?”

By following these guidelines, you can find integration partners who will drive long-term growth for your business.

# Sunbrella Introduces Marx Outdoor Drapery

[**Lindsay Brown**](https://www.wf-vision.com/profile/lbrown/)// June 26, 2026

- [![twitter](https://www.wf-vision.com/wp-content/themes/homefurnishingnews/images/x-logo+black.svg)](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?text=Sunbrella+Introduces+Marx+Outdoor+Drapery&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.wf-vision.com%2Findustry-news%2Fsunbrella-introduces-marx-outdoor-drapery%2F)

- [![linkedin](https://www.wf-vision.com/wp-content/themes/homefurnishingnews/images/linkedin.svg)](https://www.linkedin.com/shareArticle?mini=true&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.wf-vision.com%2Findustry-news%2Fsunbrella-introduces-marx-outdoor-drapery%2F&title=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.wf-vision.com%2Findustry-news%2Fsunbrella-introduces-marx-outdoor-drapery%2F)
- [![pinterest](https://www.wf-vision.com/wp-content/themes/homefurnishingnews/images/pinterest.svg)](https://pinterest.com/pin/create/button/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.wf-vision.com%2Findustry-news%2Fsunbrella-introduces-marx-outdoor-drapery%2F&media=&description=)

Outdoor spaces have become an extension of the home, and soft furnishings are helping create environments that feel more comfortable, inviting and refined. [Sunbrella](https://www.sunbrella.com/)‘s [Marx outdoor drapery](https://www.wf-vision.com/tag/marx-outdoor-drapery/ "Posts tagged with Marx outdoor drapery") combines the elegance of indoor window treatments with the durability needed for life outdoors.

Designed with a fine basketweave texture, Marx offers a soft, beautiful drape that gently filters sunlight while creating a warm atmosphere. Its casual, relaxed look makes it an easy addition to [patios](https://www.wf-vision.com/tag/patios/ "Posts tagged with patios"), [pergolas](https://www.wf-vision.com/tag/pergolas/ "Posts tagged with pergolas"), [porches](https://www.wf-vision.com/tag/porches/ "Posts tagged with porches") and other [outdoor living spaces](https://www.wf-vision.com/tag/outdoor-living-spaces/ "Posts tagged with outdoor living spaces").

![](https://www.wf-vision.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/17/2026/06/sunbrella-outdoor-drapery-marx-basalt-hero-1-225x300.jpg)

Each panel features weighted corners to help the fabric hang smoothly and evenly, while brushed stainless steel grommets provide a clean, contemporary finish.

Made with [Sunbrella](https://www.wf-vision.com/tag/sunbrella/ "Posts tagged with Sunbrella")‘s Color to the Core technology, Marx is engineered to resist fading from prolonged sun exposure while standing up to stains, [mold and mildew](https://www.wf-vision.com/tag/mold-and-mildew/ "Posts tagged with mold and mildew"). The drapery is also machine washable, bleach cleanable and specially packaged to minimize wrinkles for easy installation.

Available in eight [fade-resistant colors](https://www.wf-vision.com/tag/fade-resistant-colors/ "Posts tagged with fade-resistant colors"), Marx outdoor drapery offers homeowners and designers an easy way to add [privacy](https://www.wf-vision.com/tag/privacy/ "Posts tagged with privacy"), soften outdoor spaces and create a more comfortable outdoor environment without sacrificing durability. View the full collection [here](https://www.sunbrella.com/sunbrella-outdoor-marx-light-filtering-curtain-basalt).

![](https://www.wf-vision.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/17/2026/06/IMG_2108-300x225.jpeg)Developed in partnership with one of Sombra Shades’ premier technology partners, the new facility is located within a modern, technology-driven professional office environment designed to support the company’s rapid expansion. ![](https://www.wf-vision.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/17/2026/06/IMG_2107-300x225.jpeg)The new technology training facility is equipped to deliver both in-person and virtual education, offering dealers and partners an immersive learning experience through the latest audiovisual technology and hands-on product demonstrations. The Carrollton location further strengthens Sombra Shades’ North American operations while positioning the company for continued expansion and enhanced customer service. # From Shade to Sustainability: Inside Yardzen’s 2026 Trend Report

[**Lindsay Brown**](https://www.wf-vision.com/profile/lbrown/)// June 22, 2026

- [![twitter](https://www.wf-vision.com/wp-content/themes/homefurnishingnews/images/x-logo+black.svg)](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?text=From+Shade+to+Sustainability%3A+Inside+Yardzen%E2%80%99s+2026+Trend+Report&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.wf-vision.com%2Foutdoor-living%2Ffrom-shade-to-sustainability-inside-yardzens-2026-trend-report%2F)

- [![email](https://www.wf-vision.com/wp-content/themes/homefurnishingnews/images/email.svg)](mailto:?subject=From%20Shade%20to%20Sustainability:%20Inside%20Yardzen%E2%80%99s%202026%20Trend%20Report&body= "Share by Email")

Outdoor living continues to evolve as homeowners seek spaces that are more comfortable, functional and connected to everyday life. According to the [Yardzen 2026 Trend Report](https://yardzen.com/trend-report-2026?irclickid=whdQ3i2XcxyZRfwQC2w5tSZ5UkuT-BQZsSMM1w0&irgwc=1&afsrc=1), homeowners are increasingly prioritizing comfort, wellness, [privacy](https://www.wf-vision.com/tag/privacy/ "Posts tagged with privacy") and experiences that extend beyond traditional outdoor entertaining. From [shade structures](https://www.wf-vision.com/tag/shade-structures/ "Posts tagged with shade structures") and cooling features to native landscapes and [outdoor living rooms](https://www.wf-vision.com/tag/outdoor-living-rooms/ "Posts tagged with outdoor living rooms"), today’s backyards are being designed to support the way people live every day. Here are five trends from the report shaping the outdoor category in 2026.

**1\. Shade Becomes Essential**

Outdoor comfort is increasingly driving design decisions, and homeowners are actively seeking protection from sun and heat. [Yardzen](https://www.wf-vision.com/tag/yardzen/ "Posts tagged with yardzen") reports that requests for shade and cooling features increased 13% year over year, as homeowners prioritize comfort, refuge and microclimate control. The company also notes that privacy and climate management are becoming luxury amenities in outdoor spaces.

The trend aligns with [Houzz](https://www.wf-vision.com/tag/houzz/ "Posts tagged with Houzz")‘s 2026 Outdoor Trends Study, which found that 35% of homeowners undertaking structural outdoor projects are adding shade structures, making them the second most popular outdoor upgrade behind decks. That figure represents a 15-percentage-point increase since 2024.

**2\. The Rise of the “ [Experiential Yard](https://www.wf-vision.com/tag/experiential-yard/ "Posts tagged with experiential yard")“**

Yardzen has dubbed 2026 the “Year of the Experiential Yard.” Rather than designing around specific features, homeowners are creating outdoor environments centered on how a space feels and functions throughout the day. Spaces are being designed for morning coffee, reading, relaxing, wellness and everyday living instead of occasional entertaining.

**3\. Outdoor Living Rooms Continue to Expand**

The line between indoors and outdoors continues to blur. Houzz found that 83% of renovated outdoor spaces include a lounge or seating area, while 71% feature sofas or lounge chairs and 66% include outdoor lighting. Homeowners increasingly want outdoor spaces that function like a second living room.

**4\. Privacy Is the New Luxury**

Yardzen reports that requests for privacy-focused design elements increased 10% year over year, following a 22% increase the previous year. Rather than building outdoor spaces for entertaining large groups, homeowners are investing in quieter, more intimate environments that offer a sense of retreat and escape.

**5\. Sustainable, [Low-Maintenance Landscapes](https://www.wf-vision.com/tag/low-maintenance-landscapes/ "Posts tagged with low-maintenance landscapes") Take Root**

Homeowners continue to favor landscapes that are easier to maintain and better suited to local conditions. Yardzen found requests for [native planting](https://www.wf-vision.com/tag/native-planting/ "Posts tagged with native planting"), [pollinator gardens](https://www.wf-vision.com/tag/pollinator-gardens/ "Posts tagged with pollinator gardens") and [climate-adapted species](https://www.wf-vision.com/tag/climate-adapted-species/ "Posts tagged with climate-adapted species") increased 23% year over year. Similarly, Houzz reports that 73% of homeowners adding plants choose low-maintenance varieties, 55% select native plants and 49% opt for drought-resistant selections.

View the full report [here](https://yardzen.com/trend-report-2026?irclickid=whdQ3i2XcxyZRfwQC2w5tSZ5UkuT-BQZsSMM1w0&irgwc=1&afsrc=1).

# Hartmann&Forbes Named One of Oregon’s Best Green Workplaces

[**Lindsay Brown**](https://www.wf-vision.com/profile/lbrown/)// June 22, 2026

- [![twitter](https://www.wf-vision.com/wp-content/themes/homefurnishingnews/images/x-logo+black.svg)](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?text=Hartmann%26Forbes+Named+One+of+Oregon%E2%80%99s+Best+Green+Workplaces&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.wf-vision.com%2Findustry-news%2Fhartmannforbes-named-one-of-oregons-best-green-workplaces%2F)

Luxury window and wall covering manufacturer [Hartmann&Forbes](https://hartmannforbes.com/) has once again been recognized by [Oregon](https://www.wf-vision.com/tag/oregon/ "Posts tagged with Oregon") Business Magazine as one of the state’s 100 Best [Green Workplaces](https://www.wf-vision.com/tag/green-workplaces/ "Posts tagged with green workplaces"), earning the No. 4 spot in 2026 and marking its 14th consecutive year on the list.

The recognition highlights the company’s long-standing commitment to [sustainability](https://www.wf-vision.com/tag/sustainability/ "Posts tagged with sustainability"), a philosophy that has been central to Hartmann&Forbes since its founding.

Known for its handcrafted [window coverings](https://www.wf-vision.com/tag/window-coverings/ "Posts tagged with window coverings") and wall treatments made from rapidly [renewable natural fibers](https://www.wf-vision.com/tag/renewable-natural-fibers/ "Posts tagged with renewable natural fibers"), the company integrates environmental responsibility throughout its operations. From sourcing materials and preserving [artisan craftsmanship](https://www.wf-vision.com/tag/artisan-craftsmanship/ "Posts tagged with artisan craftsmanship") to supporting employees and industry partners, sustainability remains a key consideration in every aspect of the business.

“Being recognized among Oregon’s most environmentally responsible organizations for fourteen consecutive years is a meaningful honor,” said Michael Jones, founder of Hartmann&Forbes. “This recognition reflects the values that have guided our company from the beginning. We are grateful to our employees, clients, suppliers and partners who share in this commitment and help make this recognition possible.”

According to the company, the annual recognition serves as a reminder that sustainability is achieved through consistent action, thoughtful decision-making and a commitment to continuous improvement.

As Hartmann&Forbes celebrates this milestone, the company says it remains focused on creating products that honor both craftsmanship and the natural resources that make them possible.

To learn more about the company’s sustainability efforts, visit [hartmannforbes.com/sustainability](http://hartmannforbes.com/sustainability)
